CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
14-year-old female who presented with acute onset right-sided abdominal pain. She came home sick rubbing her abdomen and complaining of severe right-sided pain so bad she was bent over. Initial evaluation at her primary care physician was consistent with stomach virus; she received fluids and was sent home. However, she worsened significantly the next day. Follow-up ultrasound revealed one kidney larger than the other. She was subsequently evaluated at a facility in Jacksonville where she was diagnosed with an atrophic right kidney, much smaller than the left kidney. Imaging also showed cysts on the kidney and ovaries, swollen lymph nodes, and infection. She was treated at a facility in Atlanta for approximately four days and improved with resolution of vomiting. Currently, she continues to complain of abdominal pain with a burning sensation, particularly when eating. She reports dysuria with difficulty initiating urination and burning sensation with urination, particularly after consuming certain drinks such as soda. She denies hematuria.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for abdominal pain with burning sensation, especially with eating. Positive for dysuria with difficulty initiating urination and dysuria particularly with certain beverages. History of nausea and vomiting which has resolved. Denies hematuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Previously healthy. At age 4 years old, she was hospitalized 3-4 times over a couple of months, sometimes for three days at a time, with fevers and symptoms treated with fluids and antibiotics. Suspected prior kidney involvement from these infections. Prior evaluation by gastroenterology and genetics found no clinically significant mutations on genetic panel.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid 40 mg daily.
Claritin.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant for renal disease. Paternal grandfather had posterior urethral valves with obstructive neuropathy, was born with the condition, had difficulty urinating correctly, developed chronic kidney disease, had a renal transplant, and died at age 47. Paternal great-aunt has end-stage renal disease, chronic kidney disease stage 5, diabetes, and hypertension, diagnosed in adulthood. Paternal cousins have kidney disease. Maternal grandmother had breast cancer.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Active in softball. Wants to join drill team over summer. Maintains active lifestyle.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing female, alert and oriented, sitting comfortably, not in acute distress.
Cardiovascular and Pulmonary: Lungs and heart sound great.
Remaining exam: Within normal limits.

RESULTS
Kidney imaging reveals atrophic right kidney, smaller than left kidney, with left kidney appearing larger and working harder to compensate. Kidney function is normal. Blood pressure is normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Atrophic right kidney with compensatory enlargement of left kidney. Patient at higher risk for developing hypertension and proteinuria.

Annual monitoring recommended including renal ultrasound to monitor kidney size and function, urinalysis to assess for protein and blood, and blood pressure check.

Avoid non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen; use acetaminophen (Tylenol) instead.

Maintain adequate hydration with at least 2 liters of water per day, especially during athletic activities to avoid dehydration.

Continue healthy diet and active lifestyle to promote kidney health into adulthood.

Follow up with primary care physician or adult nephrologist closer to home. Does not need to return to this facility for routine follow-up.

Patient instructed to call with any questions or if symptoms worsen.
